sentences.text:
Shri Sudhanshu Vyas - Panel Lawyer for respondent/Stat
Record of trial court has been received.
Heard on admission.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 14614/2022, which is an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of custodial sentence on behalf of appellant " Deepak.

The appellant stands convicted for the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and has been sentenced to undergo 10 years RI with fine of Rs.1,000/- with usual default stipulation.
Counsel for the appellant submits that appellant was on bail during the trial and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
Looking to old pendency of the cases for consideration, final conclusion of the case would take sufficient time.
There is a strong case in favour of the appellant.
In view of the statement of the witnesses, offence is not established against the appellant.
Hence, the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence be suspended and appellant be enlarged on bail.
Per contra learned counsel for the State opposes the application and prays for its rejection.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the allegation against the appellant and also taking note of the fact that appellant was on bail during the trial, the prosecutrix (PW-1)
categorically admits in her cross examination that her engagement has been done with present appellant and she left her home with her own accord, she remained in the company of appellant for a period of 15 days, the factum of engagement was also admitted by parents of prosecutrix (PW-2 &
PW-3), final conclusion of the appeal will take long sufficient time, I find it is to be a fit case to suspend the custodial sentence of the appellant.

the execution of remaining custodial part of the sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail, till final disposal of this appeal.
Registry
is directed to list the matter for final hearing in due course.
